[MUJAHID:v2p459#4/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid identifies the deed as killing a person.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Doubling the middle radical in فعلت marks repeated or abundant action, in contrast with the un-doubled form.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The intensified pattern appears with verbs meaning repeated wounding, eating, killing, straightening, roaming, or circling.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The light form remains valid Arabic, but the doubled form is more precise when the speaker means frequent action.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الفرزدق | reports | Al-Farazdaq's line about opening and closing doors repeatedly illustrates the intensified pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur'anic form مفتحة suits repeated or abundant opening, illustrating the more marked pattern. | mentions 38:50
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur'anic expression وفجرنا الأرض عيونا likewise illustrates the pattern used for abundant action. | mentions 78:14
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابدخولفعلتعلىفعلتلايشركهفيذلكأفعلت)#683/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Action nouns such as قعدة and جلسة can name an act generally, but their derived forms mark a more specific kind; صوف and ريح similarly relate to صوفة and رائحة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Many derived verb patterns do not take a direct object; they are built intransitively, like basic verbs that do not take an object.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | انفعل has no transitive form انفعلته; forms such as انطلقت may be intransitive in their own right rather than passives of a transitive verb.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some quadriliteral and extended patterns likewise lack transitive counterparts, including احرنجمته and forms on افعنلل and افعلل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same restriction applies to quadriliteral patterns such as اطمأننت and اشمأززت; Sībawayh reports no object-taking usage for them.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some derived forms are exceptions: افعوعل and افعول can take objects, as in احلولي دماثا and اعلوطته.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · حميد الهلالي | reports | Humayd al-Hilali's verse احلولي دماثا supplies an attested transitive use of افعوعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | صعررته and a fawʿala form such as مكوكبة are also transitive because speakers formed them on quadriliteral patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Transitive derived forms are fewer than intransitive ones, as with basic patterns; verbs tend to incorporate an object just as they require an agent.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهفعلته)#690/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | اعروريت can take an object, as in اعروريت مني أمرا قبيحا, like احلولى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The regular source form for quadriliteral verbs, including triliteral roots extended to four radicals, is فعللة, as in دحرجة and زلزلة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The tāʾ in فعللة replaces the long alif found before the final consonant in forms such as زلزال; speakers also use فعلالا variants.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as الزلزال and القلقل open their first vowel like the first vowel of tafʿīl, as if the tāʾ were removed and alif added.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The فعلال form in these quadriliterals corresponds to فيعال in فاعلت, and the two forms have parallel morphological scope.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Quadriliteral verbs on استفعل and triliteral roots extended to that pattern form their sources on استفعل, as in احرنجاما and اطمئنانا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادربناتالأربعة)#695/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | الطمأنينة and القشعريرة are nominal bases, not source forms on the pattern of اطمأننت and اقشعررت, just as النبات is not the source of أنبت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | To express one occurrence of an أفعل verb, add feminine tāʾ to its regular source form, as in إعطاءة and إخراجة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same single-occurrence formation applies to افتعل and similar patterns: احترازة, انطلاقة, and استخراجة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Less common forms such as اقعنسس and اغدودن are measured by the same pattern, yielding اقعنساسة and اغديدانة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The pattern also marks one occurrence for فعلت, تفعّل, and تفاعل, as in تعذيبة, ترويحة, تقلبة, and تغافلة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For فاعل, the single occurrence uses the common source form with feminine tāʾ, as in مقاتلة and مراماة, because no shorter distinct form is available.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنظائرضربتهضربةورميتهرميةمنهذاالباب)#696/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A one-time action can also be expressed as تجاورة, parallel to تجاورا; يدعه تركة واحدة supplies another example.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An imperfect verb remains in the indicative when it occupies a noun's syntactic position; nominal governors do not affect verbs, and verbal governors do not affect nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | قد جعل يقول is understood like صار يقول, with يقول occupying the same predicate position.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | كدت and عسى avoid nominal complements because their sense resembles constructions taking أن; they use verbal clauses to preserve that meaning.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | كدت أن أفعل is allowed only in poetry; since kâda-like verbs omit أن, replacing the verb with a noun would obscure their meaning, as with جعل يقول and أخذ يقول.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The verb can occupy a subject or predicate position, as in يقول زيد ذاك and زيد يقول ذاك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Imperfect clauses also occur in positions such as an adjective, predicate, or complement, with examples including رجل يقول and حسبته ينطلق.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After هلا, يقول زيد occupies an initial nominal position; هلا governs neither nouns nor verbs, and some particles admit only verbs in such positions.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ائتني بعدما تفرغ, ما plus the verb is equivalent to the noun الفراغ; the following clause is like a clause after الذي, which governs nothing.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh rejects the claim that these verbs are raised by ابتداء alone: that would wrongly predict accusative or genitive forms wherever nouns take those cases.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In كدت أفعل and عسى يفعل, the imperfect is placed where a noun would stand after كنت; the preceding verb itself does not assign nasb or jazm.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أن زيدا جاء is a noun-like clause, and لو أن زيدا جاء means لو مجيء زيد, though the bare phrase لو مجيء زيد is not used.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابوجهدخولالرفعفيهذهالأفعالالمضارعةللأسماء)#467/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In the exclamation ما أحسن زيدا, a verb fills the slot; the corresponding noun ما محسن زيدا is not grammatical.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r4] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | “Your deed” refers to the person Moses killed.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r5] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | Pharaoh's charge that Moses was among the ungrateful means ungrateful for Pharaoh's favor of raising him.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r6] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī specifies the alleged ingratitude as denying the favor of being raised and cared for as a child.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p498/r7] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan reads “among the disbelievers” as disbelieving that Pharaoh was a god.
[FARRA:v2p279/r1] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | Pharaoh means Moses is now among those who deny his benefactor, namely Pharaoh, for raising him.
[FARRA:v2p419/r8] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | The feminine faʿlata in the reproach may instead be masculine faʿl, just as Arabic allows both feminine and masculine reference to an understood act.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p316#5/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Kāfirīn here means those ungrateful for the blessing.
[TAB-FULL:v17p554#3/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The narrative omits the connective that Moses and A

aron delivered their Lord's message; Pharaoh then asks whether he raised Moses as a child and sheltered him for years.
[TAB-FULL:v17p554#3/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Pharaoh's reference to Moses's years in his household concerns the period before Moses killed the Egyptian.
[TAB-FULL:v17p554#3/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The “deed” Pharaoh cites is Moses's killing of the Egyptian man.
[TAB-FULL:v17p554#3/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The form faʿlah here denotes a single occurrence, so its first vowel cannot be kasra with this intended meaning.
[TAB-FULL:v17p554#3/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الشعبي | rejects | Al-Shaʿbī is reported to read faʿiltu faʿlataka with kasra on the first fāʾ; al-Ṭabarī says this conflicts with the regional readers' reading.
[TAB-FULL:v17p556/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī takes Pharaoh’s words to mean that Moses belonged to Pharaoh’s religion, which Moses now criticizes.
[TAB-FULL:v17p556/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd reads this as Pharaoh’s reproach that he raised Moses as a child, yet Moses repaid him by killing one of his people and denying his kindness.
[TAB-FULL:v17p556/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says “disbeliever” means ungrateful for the favor, since Pharaoh did not know the meaning of disbelief in God.
[TAB-FULL:v17p556/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn Zayd’s reading: Pharaoh claimed to be lord and could hardly call Moses a disbeliever in Moses’ own religion; here Moses denied Pharaoh’s upbringing and kindness.
[TAB-FULL:v17p556/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Ṭabarī allows an alternative: Pharaoh might mean Moses was then a disbeliever according to the belief Moses professes now.
[TAB-FULL:v17p557/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Moses denies being an unbeliever: he had acted while misguided, and Ibn Masʿūd's wording reads “among the ignorant.”
[ZAJJAJ:v4p85/r6] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | prefers | The fatḥa reading فعلتك is better and more common, treating the killing as a single occurrence; al-Shaʿbi’s kasra reading فعلتك describes the manner of the act, illustrated by the distinction between a sitting once and a way of sitting.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p85/r7] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | وأنت من الكافرين may mean that Moses was ungrateful for Pharaoh’s favor, or that he was a disbeliever by committing the killing.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid says the deed Pharaoh recalled was the killing of a person.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda likewise identifies the deed as the killing Moses committed.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r5] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī understands “among the disbelievers” as Pharaoh accusing Moses of leaving Pharaoh's religion, which Moses had criticized.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r6] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Pharaoh meant Moses had denied Pharaoh's favor in raising him.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r7] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · محمد بن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Isḥāq recounts Pharaoh framing his raising of Moses as a favor, then accusing him of killing one of Pharaoh's followers.
[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2753/r8] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم | reports | ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says Pharaoh asks whether killing one of his people and denying his favor is how Moses repays being raised in his household.
[NAHHAS:v3p175/r11] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | The clause may be circumstantial: you killed the person while in this state.
[NAHHAS:v3p175/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Alternatively, Pharaoh means Moses is now ungrateful for his favor because he is demanding the release of the Israelites.
[IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p127/r2] IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB, d. 392 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbī reads فِعْلَتك with kasra on fāʾ; Ibn Jinnī explains فعلة as the state or manner of an act, as in posture, sitting, walking, or eating, and compares مصدر alternations such as نشدته نشدا.
[THALABI:v7p160/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbi alone is reported to have read “your deed” with a kasra on the fāʾ.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The deed Pharaoh recalls was Moses’s killing of a man.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r5] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī says “one of the unbelievers” means that Moses followed Pharaoh’s religion, which Moses did not call unbelief.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · محمد بن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Isḥāq says Pharaoh calls Moses ungrateful for Pharaoh’s beneficence and favor.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس والمفسرون | reports | The act was Moses' killing of the Copt.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الحسن والسدي | reports | One reading is that Moses disbelieved in Pharaoh's god and followed the religion he now criticizes.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن زيد، مقاتل، عطاء، العوفي عن ابن عباس | reports | Another reading is ingratitude for Pharaoh's favors: he raised Moses and treated him well, yet Moses killed one of his people.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · العوفي عن ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh did not understand disbelief in the Lord as the charge here.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | prefers | Al-Farrāʾ selects ingratitude for Pharaoh's favor of raising Moses.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p33/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل المعاني | reports | Pharaoh's reply belittles the caller to God out of arrogance, redirecting the discussion from its proper subject.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:18-20/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Pharaoh identifies the deed as killing the Copt and accuses Moses of denying the favor Pharaoh bestowed on him.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p14/r1] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | A noun is complete when it has a feature that prevents annexation, such as dual or plural nūn, tanwīn, estimated tanwīn, or an existing annexation; he cites «ملء الأرض ذهبا». | mentions 3:91
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p14/r2] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Nouns attach to verbs as subjects and as objects, including direct objects, adverbs, accompaniment, and causal objects; he illustrates the latter with 4:114. | mentions 4:114
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p14/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Some nouns are governed like objects despite not being direct objects, including the predicate of kāna, circumstantial accusatives, tamyīz, and the exception.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p14/r4] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Prepositions mediate between a verb and a noun it cannot govern directly; the accompaniment wāw and إلا likewise mediate, though the verb rather than the particle supplies accusative government.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p184/r1] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The poet frames «May God punish the liar» as a response to an imagined question about an accusation of lying, making it a fresh assertion.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p184/r2] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | In the reply «I am ill», the poet anticipates the unspoken follow-up «what is wrong?» and answers it with constant sleeplessness and grief.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p184/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Al-Mutanabbī denies that the winds erased the dwelling, then supplies the implied answer to who did erase it: the one who drove and led them.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p184/r4] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Al-Walīd ibn Yazīd uses the same pattern: after saying the house faded, he imagines the question of what erased it and names the agent.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p184/r5] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | When a question is explicit, its answer may omit the verb; when the question is only implied by context, the verb must be stated because the listener otherwise cannot recover it.
[JISHUMI:v7p5342/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قراءة العامة | reports | The common fatḥa reading of faʿlata means the deed was done once.
[JISHUMI:v7p5342/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbī reads faʿlata with a kasra, meaning a manner or instance of action, like saying I sat a sitting.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r20] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The deed Pharaoh mentions was Moses' killing of the Egyptian.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r21] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن والسدي | reports | “Among the disbelievers” means disbelieving in the religion Pharaoh's people followed, which Pharaoh uses to blame Moses.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r22] JISHUMI, d. 494 · ابن عباس وابن زيد وأبو علي | reports | Another interpretation is that Pharaoh meant Moses was ungrateful for Pharaoh's favor and upbringing.
[JISHUMI:v7p5344/r23] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Pharaoh may have echoed a statement he heard from Moses denouncing him and his people as disbelievers.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p109/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The deed Pharaoh cites is Moses’s killing of the Copt.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p109/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · الحسن والسدي | reports | Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī take “you were among the unbelievers” to mean Moses rejected his deity and followed Pharaoh’s religion.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p109/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أكثر المفسرين | reports | Most exegetes say Pharaoh means Moses denied Pharaoh’s favor and the right of his upbringing by killing one of Pharaoh’s people.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p109/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · العوفي عن ابن عباس | reports | Al-ʿAwfī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Pharaoh did not know the concept of unbelief in divine lordship.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p227/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Faʿaltaka with fatḥa means the single act; al-Shaʿbī reads fiʿlataka with kasra, meaning the manner or form of the act.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p227/r15] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads wa-anta mina al-kāfirīn as saying Moses was a disbeliever when he killed the Copt, since that person could not lawfully be killed.
